items.title: Newest Sources of Western Zhou History: Inscribed Bronze Vessels, 2000–2010
items.note: Surveys inscribed bronzes found in 2000–2010, the new dated inscriptions against which any reconstructed Western Zhou calendar is now tested.

items.title: The Nivison Annals: Selected Works of David S. Nivison on Early Chinese Chronology, Astronomy, and Historiography
items.who: D. S. Nivison (ed. A. C. Schwartz)
items.note: Collected papers, including a record of the Nivison–Shaughnessy debate on the Bamboo Annals and Nivison's later arguments for a conquest in the 1040s.

items.title: Yinqi wenyuan (殷契文渊) oracle-bone inscription data platform
items.note: Free online corpus of some 230,000 oracle-bone images and 150 publications, the base for late Shang reign sequences and eclipse records; upgraded in 2024.

items.title: Radiocarbon Dating of Oracle Bones of Late Shang Period in Ancient China
items.who: K. Liu, X. Wu, Z. Guo et al.
items.note: Sequenced AMS dates on oracle bones assigned to successive kings place Wu Ding at about 1254–1197 BC and the end of Shang around 1041 BC.

items.title: Xia Shang Zhou duandai gongcheng baogao (夏商周断代工程报告)
items.note: Final report of the state chronology project, launched in July 2022, keeping 1046 BCE (dated to 20 January) for the conquest as in the 2000 summary.

items.title: The Chronology of Western Zhou
items.note: Rebuilds the lunar-phase terms from fully dated bronzes and argues for an initial campaign in 1046 and Zhòu's defeat in 1044 BCE, rejecting the current Bamboo Annals.

items.title: The Xia Shang Zhou duandai gongcheng baogao and Its Chronology of the Western Zhou Dynasty
items.note: Review of the Project's 2022 final report, arguing that bronzes published since 2000 show its Western Zhou absolute chronology to be fundamentally flawed and that the report left it uncorrected.

items.title: A View from the Countryside: Radiocarbon Chronology for Zaolinhetan of the Pre-Zhou Culture in Early Dynastic China
items.who: X. Li, W. Liu, Y. Xu et al.
items.note: High-resolution dates from a pre-Zhou settlement in the Jing valley show abandonment around 1100 BCE as Zhouyuan expanded, constraining the pre-conquest sequence.

items.title: A modeling radiocarbon dating for the founding of Yan Vassal State in Western Zhou Dynasty
items.who: X. Ouyang, X. Wu, J. Wang et al.
items.note: Wiggle-matched skeletal samples from a Liulihe tomb whose bronze records the founding of Yan's capital give a death date of about 1045–1010 BC, close to the conquest.
